ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a rectangle, with the width marked at the top as 6 cm. Inside the rectangle there are 6 identical circles, arranged in a tight triangular arrangement: the top row has 3 circles tangent to one another, and their tops touch the upper side of the rectangle; the middle row has 2 circles embedded below the gaps between the circles in the top row; the bottommost 1 circle is located below the two middle circles, and its bottom touches the lower side of the rectangle. Reasoning: Because the top row of 3 identical circles exactly spans the 6 cm width of the rectangle, the sum of 3 diameters is 6 cm, the diameter of each circle is 6/3 = 2 cm, and the radius r = 1 cm. The length of the line segment connecting the centers of tangent circles in two adjacent rows is equal to the sum of two radii, namely 2 cm. The centers of three mutually tangent equal circles form an equilateral triangle with side length 2 cm, so the vertical distance between the centers of circles in two adjacent rows is the height of this equilateral triangle, namely sqrt(2^2 - 1^2) = sqrt(3) cm. From the top of the rectangle to the centers of the top-row circles there is 1 radius, namely 1 cm; from the centers of the top-row circles to the centers of the middle-row circles it descends sqrt(3) cm; from the centers of the middle-row circles to the center of the bottom-row circle it descends another sqrt(3) cm; from the center of the bottom-row circle to the bottom of the rectangle there is still 1 radius, namely 1 cm. Therefore the height of the rectangle is 1 + sqrt(3) + sqrt(3) + 1 = 2sqrt(3) + 2 cm.

raw_record.question_text: Six identical circles fit together tightly in a rectangle of width $6 \mathrm{~cm}$ as shown. What is the height, in $\mathrm{cm}$, of the rectangle?

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: the rectangle contains 6 congruent circles in a triangular packing, with 3 circles in the top row touching the top side and spanning the full width, 2 circles nestled below the gaps, and 1 circle at the bottom. From the text, the rectangle width is 6 cm. Since the top row shows three equal diameters fitting exactly across the width, each diameter is 6/3 = 2 cm, so r = 1 cm. Draw line segments between centers of tangent circles in adjacent rows. Three mutually tangent equal circles form an equilateral triangle of side 2r = 2, so the vertical drop between neighboring rows is the altitude of that equilateral triangle: sqrt(2^2 - 1^2) = sqrt(3). There are two such row drops, plus one radius above the top centers and one radius below the bottom center. Height = 1 + sqrt(3) + sqrt(3) + 1 = 2sqrt(3)+2.
